advantages: Returns `true` only when every element is `null`, making it a strict “all match” guard.
Rejects non-arrays and empty arrays by returning `false`, preventing accidental truthy results on invalid input.
It works well as a precondition check before processing data that must be entirely `null`.

parameterDescriptions.array: The input array to check for `null` elements.

shortDescription: Checks whether all elements in the given `array` are `null`.
typeScriptHint: Use `areNull` when you need a strict check that an input is a non-empty array and every element is exactly `null` (not `undefined`, not falsy values).
useCase: Validate that a dataset column, API field list, or placeholder array contains only `null` values before applying logic that assumes all entries are intentionally empty.
